blocks.text: You can add session attributes related to the user's session in Authentication Service, so they can be made available to the linked Zscaler services. Session attributes (system-defined or custom) that are mapped with identity provider (IdP) attributes are sent to Zscaler services (e.g., Internet & SaaS (ZIA), Private Access (ZPA)) with the values received from the external IdP as part of SAML assertions or OIDC tokens.

Session attributes are equivalent to SAML attributes supported in Private Access when a Private Access tenant is linked with Authentication Service for admins and users. The session attributes created in Authentication Service] are used in Private Access access policies and system-defined device attributes (is_device_managed, is_device_compliant, and is_device_domain_joined) are used in Internet & SaaS Identity Proxies. If you are configuring an identity proxy for cloud apps, you must map the is_device_managed attribute to an IdP attribute, and then configure the managed devices settings in Internet & SaaS. To learn more, see Configuring the Zscaler Identity Proxy for Cloud Apps.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Administration > Authentication > Attributes.
On the Attributes page, click the Session Attribute tab.
The Add Session Attribute drawer appears.
In the Add Session Attribute drawer, add the following details:
Attribute Name: Enter the session attribute name.
Display Name: Enter the display name for the attribute.
Description: Enter a description for the attribute.
Data Type: Select the type of data (String, Integer, Boolean, Date, or Decimal) that must be entered for this attribute.

blocks.text: You can add multiple session attributes to Authentication Service by importing a CSV file.
To import a CSV file that contains a list of session attributes:

blocks.item: On the Attributes page, click the Session Attribute tab.
In the Import Attributes window, click the Download Sample link to download a sample CSV file.
Add the attributes to the CSV file and save it in your local folder.
Click Browse to locate the saved CSV file, then click Open.
The records are displayed in the Import Attributes window.
Review the list, then click Close.
The attributes are added to the existing list and displayed on the Attributes page.
